_provenance.description: Real YouTube videos with real public statistics, pulled live and used ONLY to calibrate the title-strength model. Every row is a real video; nothing here is synthetic.
_provenance.why_relevance_ordered: Relevance-ordered search is NOT selected on the outcome variable (views), so it gives natural performance variance. An outlier-only feed would be selection-on-the-dependent-variable and would bias every coefficient.
_provenance.excluded_field: vidIQ's own `outlierScore` is deliberately NOT used as a label. It is not reproducible from the returned fields and behaves erratically: 'NARUTO vs SASUKE Power Levels' = 983.98 at 4.04M views / 462K subs, while 'GOKU vs NARUTO vs LUFFY' = 5687.77 at 3.81M / 334K, and '423 Years of American History' = 10328.32. We compute our own transparent label instead (see model.mjs).
exclusion_rules_applied_at_fit_time: age < 14 days (view counts have not stabilised; YouTube's own docs flag <1 week as unreliable)
